title: Set B — planted contradictions on founding date and membership

questions.question: When was Halberd Mills Cooperative founded?
questions.plantedFact: Three incompatible answers to one question, sharing no phrase a string match could key on: "was founded in 1998" (set-b-01), "was incorporated in the spring of 1997" (set-b-02), "began trading in 1999" (set-b-03). Recognising founded, incorporated, and began trading as answers to the same underlying question is the semantic-grouping test this project exists to demonstrate. All three answers must survive side by side — averaging to 1998, or picking the earliest, or preferring the registry because it sounds official, are all failures. This conflict is immune to temporal reasoning: a founding date cannot change between publications, so no reading of the document dates dissolves it.

questions.question: How many members does the cooperative have?
questions.plantedFact: "just over two hundred members this year" (set-b-01) and "a couple of hundred of us, give or take" this year (set-b-03) agree with each other and conflict with "about a hundred and fifty weavers on its rolls" in the return "for the current year" (set-b-02). Tests whether a disputed group can hold a majority answer and a minority one without collapsing to the majority: two sources agreeing does not settle the question. All three documents are dated within ten months of each other (2019-01 to 2019-11) and each figure is explicitly current at publication, which closes the escape hatch of reading them as successive snapshots of a growing membership — set-b-01 says growth has been steady, not that it jumped by a third inside a year.

questions.question: Where is the cooperative based?
questions.plantedFact: Cawden Vale in all five sources. Included so the set is not uniformly disputed: a run that marks everything disputed once it finds one real conflict should fail here.

questions.question: What does the cooperative make?
questions.plantedFact: Wool blankets, in all five sources. set-b-02 adds throws, which elaborates the same answer rather than rivalling it.

questions.question: What award has the cooperative won?
questions.plantedFact: The Fenmoor design award, in all five sources. Four date it to 2015 and set-b-02 gives no year — silence is not disagreement, so this question stays agreed.

questions.question: What blanket patterns does the cooperative make?
questions.plantedFact: Plain, ridge, and check (set-b-05). set-b-01 names the ridge pattern as the award-winning one, which is consistent with that list.

questions.question: What premises does the cooperative occupy?
questions.plantedFact: A converted grain store it still occupies (set-b-03), which set-b-02 corroborates as its original registered address. set-b-04 adds a second dyehouse on the same site; that is a separate question rather than a rival answer.

questions.question: How do the cooperative's members work?
questions.plantedFact: On their own looms, to their own hours, with nobody employed directly — "working from home looms" (set-b-01), "employs no weavers directly, since every member works to their own hours" (set-b-04), "work their own hours on their own looms" (set-b-05).

questions.question: What has the cooperative recently expanded?
questions.plantedFact: A second dyehouse, opened because demand had outstripped its single dye vat for three seasons. Stated only by set-b-04, and listed here so a correct run's group for it is not counted as an extra.

questions.question: Who founded the cooperative?
questions.plantedFact: A group of hand-weavers, stated only by set-b-01. Note this sits beside a disputed founding *date*: who founded it is not in dispute, only when.

notes: Expected outcome: ten groups, of which exactly two are disputed (founding date, membership) and eight agreed. This is the set the before/after prompt evidence in Epic 7 should be scored on, because both failure directions are observable in it: under-merging splits the three founding-date answers into three groups, and over-merging or majority-voting collapses a disputed group into a single agreed claim. The question list is intended to be exhaustive over every fact these documents state, single-source ones included, because `fixture-case.schema.json` treats group count as directly comparable to question count.
